title: German court rules that AI music firm violated copyrights
facts: The Munich Regional Court ruled that US-based AI music generator Suno AI violated copyright laws.
The Munich Regional Court ordered Suno AI to disclose illicit revenues generated from copyrighted material.
German licensing agency GEMA initiated the copyright infringement lawsuit against Suno AI in January 2025.
Tobias Holzmüller serves as the Chief Executive Officer of GEMA.
GEMA represents more than 95,000 composers, songwriters, and music publishers in Germany.
GEMA represents over 2 million rights holders globally.
GEMA won a copyright lawsuit against OpenAI regarding unauthorized song lyric reproduction in 2025.
Martin Senftleben serves as a professor of intellectual property law at Amsterdam Law School.
GEMA demonstrated copyright infringement by prompting Suno AI with lyrics from songs including 'Daddy Cool' and 'Cheri Cheri Lady'.
GEMA tested Suno AI using original lyrics from Alphaville's 'Forever Young' and Lou Bega's 'Mambo No. 5'.
Suno AI acknowledged that original copyrighted songs cited in the lawsuit were included in its AI training dataset.
Users across Suno AI's platform generate approximately 7 million audio tracks per day.
Approximately 75,000 AI-generated songs from Suno AI are uploaded to streaming platforms daily.
Suno AI announced it would evaluate legal options including an appeal against the Munich Regional Court ruling.
Suno AI allows users to generate structured musical compositions with vocals and instruments from text prompts.
